title: Zha-Chong Shi-San-Wei Pill inhibits ferroptosis in cerebral ischemia via bioinformatics and experimental confirmation methods.
authors: Shang, Jinfeng; Chen, Wenbin; Wei, Wanting; Wang, Bohong; Song, Qi; Bai, Meirong; Liu, Xin
one_liner_zh: 该研究聚焦中药复方通过HIF-1alpha/HO-1通路抑制脑缺血铁死亡，虽含分子对接和MD模拟，但核心是药理机制而非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Ischemic stroke (IS), accounting for approximately 85% of all stroke cases, is a cerebrovascular catastrophe that inflicts cerebral parenchymal damage through multifactorial mechanisms, resulting in millions of deaths and long-term neurological disabilities worldwide. Zha-Chong Shi-San-Wei Pill (ZCSSW), a compound formulation derived from a synergistic blend of Mongolian medicinal herbs, has demonstrated significant therapeutic efficacy in managing IS. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aims to investigate whether ZCSSW inhibits ferroptosis in cerebral ischemia (CI) via the hypoxia-inducible factor-1alpha (HIF-1alpha)/heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1) pathway. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A network pharmacology analysis integrating component identification and database screening was conducted to explore the anti-CI effects of ZCSSW. Molecular docking was performed to validate interactions between crucial bioactive constituents and core targets. A permanent middle cerebral artery occlusion (pMCAO, 12 h) model in rats and an oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD, 12 h) model in PC12 cells were established to elucidate the molecular mechanisms. Pharmacodynamic evaluations in pMCAO rats included tetrazolium red staining for cerebral infarction quantification, neurological deficit scoring and hematoxylin-eosin staining for histopathological assessment. Cellular viability under OGD was measured using the cell counting kit-8. Mechanistic investigations employed transmission electron microscopy for ultrastructural analysis. Protein expression levels of HIF-1alpha, HO-1, ferritin heavy (FTH1), transferrin (TF) and transferrin receptor (TFRC) were quantified via immunohistochemistry, Western blot and immunofluorescence. Pharmacological modulation using erastin (a ferroptosis inducer) and lificiguat (YC-1, a HIF-1alpha inhibitor) to assess the role of the HIF-1alpha/HO-1 pathway in CI-associated ferroptosis. Molecular interaction techniques including molecular dynamics simulation, cellular thermal shift assay, drug affinity responsive target stability and co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) assays were used to validate the binding of core ZCSSW components to the HIF-1alpha/HO-1 pathway and their regulatory effects on ferroptosis. RESULTS: Network analysis identified 84 bioactive constituents in ZCSSW targeting 1000 CI-related proteins, with the ferroptosis pathway as the central regulatory mechanism. Liquiritigenin showed strong binding affinity to HIF-1alpha. Optimal doses of ZCSSW (162 mg/kg in vivo and 2.5% medicated serum in vitro) significantly reduced cerebral infarction volume, neuronal loss and neurological scores while attenuating mitochondrial ultrastructural damage. ZCSSW intervention modulated differential metabolite profiles, also attenuated reactive oxygen species and ferrous ion accumulation. This correlated with downregulation of HIF-1alpha, HO-1, TF and TFRC and upregulation of FTH1. Erastin counteracted ZCSSW's therapeutic effects while YC-1 synergistically enhanced its efficacy. Molecular interaction experiments confirmed tight binding of crucial ZCSSW components to the HIF-1alpha/HO-1 pathway, enhancing protein stability. Co-IP assays verified a direct HIF-1alpha/HO-1 interaction. Further experiments demonstrated that these vital components (liquiritigenin and glycyrrhizin) alleviated ferroptosis in rat CI injury and in OGD-injured PC12 cells by modulating the HIF-1alpha/HO-1 pathway. CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates through pharmacological and mechanistic validation that ZCSSW exerts anti-ferroptosis effects in CI through inhibiting HIF-1alpha/HO-1 pathway. The findings highlight the therapeutic synergy between antioxidative stress modulation and enhanced mitophagy in mitigating CI pathogenesis.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：缺血性卒中（IS）约占所有卒中病例的85%，是一种通过多因素机制造成脑实质损伤的脑血管灾难性疾病，在全球范围内导致数百万人死亡和长期神经功能障碍。扎冲十三味丸（ZCSSW）是一种由蒙古草药协同配伍而成的复方制剂，在治疗IS方面显示出显著的疗效。研究目的：本研究旨在探讨ZCSSW是否通过缺氧诱导因子-1α（HIF-1α）/血红素加氧酶-1（HO-1）通路抑制脑缺血（CI）中的铁死亡。材料与方法：采用整合成分鉴定和数据库筛选的网络药理学分析，探讨ZCSSW的抗CI作用。通过分子对接验证关键生物活性成分与核心靶点之间的相互作用。建立大鼠永久性大脑中动脉闭塞（pMCAO，12小时）模型和PC12细胞氧糖剥夺（OGD，12小时）模型，以阐明分子机制。pMCAO大鼠的药效学评估包括四唑红染色用于脑梗死定量、神经功能缺损评分和苏木精-伊红染色用于组织病理学评估。使用细胞计数试剂盒-8测量OGD条件下的细胞活力。机制研究采用透射电子显微镜进行超微结构分析。通过免疫组织化学、Western blot和免疫荧光定量检测HIF-1α、HO-1、铁蛋白重链（FTH1）、转铁蛋白（TF）和转铁蛋白受体（TFRC）的蛋白表达水平。使用erastin（一种铁死亡诱导剂）和lificiguat（YC-1，一种HIF-1α抑制剂）进行药理学调节，以评估HIF-1α/HO-1通路在CI相关铁死亡中的作用。采用分子动力学模拟、细胞热位移分析、药物亲和力响应靶点稳定性和共免疫沉淀（Co-IP）等分子相互作用技术，验证ZCSSW核心成分与HIF-1α/HO-1通路的结合及其对铁死亡的调节作用。结果：网络分析鉴定出ZCSSW中84种生物活性成分靶向1000个CI相关蛋白，其中铁死亡通路是核心调节机制。甘草素对HIF-1α表现出强结合亲和力。ZCSSW的最佳剂量（体内162 mg/kg和体外2.5%含药血清）显著减少了脑梗死体积、神经元丢失和神经功能评分，同时减轻了线粒体超微结构损伤。ZCSSW干预调节了差异代谢物谱，并减弱了活性氧和亚铁离子积累。这与HIF-1α、HO-1、TF和TFRC的下调以及FTH1的上调相关。Erastin抵消了ZCSSW的治疗效果，而YC-1协同增强了其疗效。分子相互作用实验证实了ZCSSW关键成分与HIF-1α/HO-1通路的紧密结合，增强了蛋白稳定性。Co-IP实验验证了HIF-1α/HO-1的直接相互作用。进一步实验表明，这些关键成分（甘草素和甘草酸）通过调节HIF-1α/HO-1通路，减轻了大鼠CI损伤和OGD损伤PC12细胞中的铁死亡。结论：本研究通过药理学和机制验证表明，ZCSSW通过抑制HIF-1α/HO-1通路在CI中发挥抗铁死亡作用。研究结果强调了抗氧化应激调节与增强线粒体自噬在减轻CI发病机制中的治疗协同作用。
